title: How a stablecoin actually keeps its dollar value (most of the time)
one_idea: A stablecoin is a prepaid digital contract — you pay dollars upfront and the issuer holds assets in reserve, but unlike a prepaid contract, reserves may be fractional, the peg can break, and redemption is not guaranteed.

analogy.limitation: Unlike a prepaid contract, a stablecoin's reserves may be fractional, the peg can break, and redemption is not guaranteed.

audience_misconception: Most viewers think stablecoins hold a guaranteed $1 value like a bank account, but the peg depends on market trust and reserves may be incomplete.

packaging.title_rationale: Leads with the concrete prepaid contract idea but adds the critical qualifier that sets this apart from misleading analogies
packaging.description:
A stablecoin is a prepaid digital contract that holds your dollars at approximately one dollar. Think of it like a prepaid contract — you pay upfront, the issuer holds reserves, you get a token. But unlike a prepaid contract, the peg can break, reserves may be fractional, and redemption is not guaranteed. The Fed just opened public comment on rules for who gets to issue them.

Sources: Federal Reserve press release, September 2026 — https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/bcreg20260924a.htm

concepts.name: stablecoin
concepts.definition: a cryptocurrency designed to maintain an approximately $1 price by holding dollar-equivalent assets in reserve, though reserves may be fractional and the peg is market-dependent rather than guaranteed

concepts.name: reserve backing
concepts.definition: permissible assets held by the stablecoin issuer meant to equal the value of tokens in circulation, though many stablecoins hold only fractional reserves

concepts.name: prepaid contract
concepts.definition: money paid upfront that guarantees a fixed rate or service; the funds sit in reserve until the contract is fulfilled

concepts.name: peg
concepts.definition: the target exchange rate of a stablecoin to the dollar; maintained by market trust and reserve quality rather than guaranteed contract

original_contribution: Explains stablecoins through the prepaid contract metaphor as one beat only, then shows exactly where the analogy misleads: fractional reserves, peg instability, and no guaranteed redemption — connecting these real risks to the Fed's new framework.
director_notes:
Format chosen: versus — reason: comparing prepaid contracts to stablecoins maps onto the vs structure, but the key revelation is where the analogy fails.
Analogy approach: prepaid contract used as ONE-BEAT metaphor in s2 only; limitation spoken in s3 and reinforced in s5 and s6.
Fix applied: removed the STABLECOIN visual term from s2 (it was the first illustration scene and the analogy beat, which violates term_after_picture). Moved the STABLECOIN on-screen term reveal to s5 (beat: term), with keyframe reframed to a clean token so the label matches the visual. PEG demoted from term to idea (still explained in narration and shown by the tilted dollar in the s5 motion) to stay within the audience's 3-term jargon budget (RESERVE BACKING + STABLECOIN = 2 visual terms).
Open loops: [What is a stablecoin opened at s1; paid at s5 / Where does the analogy break opened at s2; paid at s3 / Why is the Fed writing rules opened at s4; paid at s5]
Unresolved QA warnings: scene durations warn at 8s ceiling (audience scene_len_sec vs length_sec conflict; 6 scenes at 2.6 wps yields 72s, exceeding 8s/scene). Total sits comfortably inside the 25-90s error band.
Claims to verify before approval: None — claims match exactly what the Fed press release supports. Fractional-reserve and peg-break risks are stated as general market conditions, not sourced claims.
